note: Every source here is chosen for one property above all others: it does not change. Standards documents that were frozen on publication, a 1989 proposal kept as a historical record, and specification files that have not been touched in years. A clue whose page drifts does not produce a wrong verdict - it produces UNDETERMINED and costs the player nothing - but it does waste consensus, so drift is designed out rather than handled.
authoring_rules: The anchor must never contain the answer. It is public in the clue view, so an anchor that leaks the answer turns the clue into a giveaway.
The anchor sits immediately before the material, because the window runs forward from it.
The answer pattern is checked on chain before any model is called. It is the cheap filter that keeps the answer space near binary and stops a player burning tribunal budget on an essay.

The source URL is public. It has to be - it is on chain, and claiming otherwise would be a claimed-behaviour mismatch. The race is about solving faster with the same information, not about privileged information.

clues.title: Short and Stout
clues.riddle: On the first of April 1998 the IETF published a standard for controlling coffee pots over HTTP. It reserves an error for the case where you ask a teapot to brew. The document says the resulting entity body MAY be short and one other thing. Give that word.
clues.anchor: any attempt to brew coffee with a teapot
clues.hint: The joke is a nursery rhyme.

clues.title: By Air
clues.riddle: A 1990 memo specifies the transmission of IP datagrams by pigeon. It gives a typical maximum transmission unit, and the unit of measure is not bytes. Give the number only.
clues.hint: Milligrams. And it is a power of two.

clues.title: Number One
clues.riddle: The very first Request for Comments was circulated from UCLA in April 1969. Give the surname of the person whose name is on it.
clues.hint: He later chaired the Network Working Group itself.

clues.title: Still Served
clues.riddle: The oldest page still served from CERN describes the project in a single sentence. It calls it a wide-area something information retrieval initiative. Give the missing word.
clues.hint: Not hypertext. The broader word that includes it.

clues.title: Nodes and Arcs
clues.riddle: A CERN proposal dated 12 November 1990 opens by describing a way to link and access information as a web of nodes in which the user can browse at will. Give the name of this approach in one word.
clues.anchor: the attached document describes in more detail
clues.hint: Read the definition after the addressees.

clues.title: Reserved
clues.riddle: Some domain names can never be registered because a standards document set them aside for use in documentation. Give the number of the RFC that first reserved them.
clues.hint: There are two RFCs named on that page. You want the earlier one.

clues.title: Closed Ecosystem
clues.riddle: The current JSON specification makes one encoding mandatory for text exchanged between systems that are not part of a closed ecosystem. Name it.
clues.hint: It is the one everything else lost to.

clues.title: Arbitrarily Defined
clues.riddle: The TCP specification needs a bound on how long a segment can survive in the network, and admits the value it picks is arbitrary. It is given in minutes. Give the number.
clues.anchor: msl maximum segment lifetime, the time a tcp segment
clues.hint: Small. The TIME-WAIT state waits twice as long.

clues.title: The Standard Everything Copied
clues.riddle: The Ethereum token standard lists a handful of methods, and marks three of them optional. One of the three exists purely to say how far a balance can be divided. Name that method.
clues.answer_form: one word, the method name, lowercase
clues.hint: Every wallet reads it before showing you a balance.

clues.title: Mixed Case
clues.riddle: Ethereum addresses are case-insensitive, so a proposal smuggled a checksum into the choice of upper and lower case letters. Name the hash function that decides which letters are capitalised.
clues.anchor: in english, convert the address to hex
clues.answer_form: the name of a hash function
clues.hint: Not SHA-256. The one Ethereum uses everywhere else.

clues.title: Eleven Bits
clues.riddle: A mnemonic scheme splits your entropy into equal groups of bits, and each group encodes a number used as an index into a wordlist. Give the largest number that index can take.
clues.anchor: appended to the end of the initial entropy
clues.hint: Eleven bits per group. The range starts at zero.

clues.title: Home
clues.riddle: The chain you are racing on forbids one ordinary Python container in contract storage and names a replacement for it. Give the name of the replacement, one word.
clues.anchor: dict[k, v] needs to be replaced with
clues.hint: You have been running on it the whole time.
